# Overview of Session 2 {#sec-s2}

In Session 1 you calculated forward: from cost to price, from net to gross. Business questions often run the other way round. You know the result you need (no loss, a target profit, a revenue goal) and you are looking for the number that gets you there: how many units, which price. That is what equations are for.

::: {.goals}
Goals

After this session you can:

- turn a business question into an equation and say what the unknown stands for;
- solve linear equations step by step, and check the solution;
- rearrange a formula to get the variable you need;
- solve quadratic equations with factorising and with the quadratic formula, and use the discriminant to tell how many solutions there are;
- calculate break-even volumes and target prices, and judge whether an answer makes sense.
:::

## Before class

- [ ] Work through the chapters of this session: @sec-equations to @sec-quadratic (about 75 minutes, videos included).
- [ ] Try the questions in @sec-s2-practice (about 20 minutes).
- [ ] Take **Entry quiz 2** on Moodle before the deadline.

**If you want more explanation or practice** (optional), the same topics are covered in @olivier2023, sec. 2.5, pp. 46–56, and sec. 5.2, pp. 157–164, and in @stitz2013, sec. 2.3, pp. 188–207; also in @mazur2021, sec. 2.1–2.5, pp. 167–270. In German: @gundlach2024, sec. 1.3, pp. 21–22.

## In class

| Time | What happens |
|-------------|------------------------------------------------------------|
| 0:00–0:20   | The quiz questions most people found hard |
| 0:20–1:20   | Problem set A in your group: your break-even volume and the price for a target profit, by hand |
| 1:20–1:35   | Break |
| 1:35–2:35   | Problem set B: a profit model with two break-even points, and what it means when there is no solution |

Could not prepare? Start with the [catch-up sheet](catch-up.qmd) and join your group for problem set B.
